transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Sanjay Iyer (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Valencia Head of ML), Tom Reed (Valencia Platform Eng), Nina Patel (Valencia Security)

[00:00] Jamie Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we all see the calendar item, uh quick intros 
- i'm jamie, AE at Redwood, and sanjay is our systems engineer who will go into perf and migration details.
[00:08] Alicia Gomez: hey hi, thanks, i'm alicia, head of ml at valencia. we're exploring moving some workloads off openai to reduce costs and to get more control over data residency.
[00:14] Tom Reed: tom here, platform, mostly concerned about throughput and integrating into our k8s infra or whether we need a separate cluster.
[00:20] Nina Patel: nina, security. SOC2 is mandatory for us, also need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs retained for a year.
[00:28] Jamie Park: great, that's helpful. high-level Redwood offers hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (vpc/on-prem). today i'd love to understand your workloads, qps, typical seq len, and what parity means for you.
[00:40] Alicia Gomez: quick context we use openai for most generation, but for cost-sensitive batch runs we also host vLLM on gpus (tgi experiments too). main concerns: output parity (we run a lot of evals), latency at 99th percentile for interactive features, and compliance for some EU customers.
[00:58] Sanjay Iyer: got it. when you say parity are you validating against specific models or prompt sets?
[01:03] Alicia Gomez: yes, we have a 2k prompt eval set (classification + multi-turn chat) outputs must match baseline quality within our heuristic and BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics. Also hallucination rate is measured.
[01:15] Tom Reed: on infra: current vLLM setup is on prem-ish using k8s + gpu nodes, but ops is brittle; we lose throughput when kv cache warms, and seq len spikes cause high latency. we want more predictable tails.
[01:32] Sanjay Iyer: that aligns with a lot of customers. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with autoscale and strict SLOs. we also do automatic kv/prefix caching and sequence-aware batching to keep tails stable.
[01:46] Jamie Park: curious where are most users hosted? us? eu?
[01:49] Alicia Gomez: split 60% us, 40% eu; some data residency needs for a handful of enterprise customers in frankfurt.
[01:57] Nina Patel: also need SAML SSO + RBAC for model access and audit logs that tie back to our user ids.
[02:04] Sanjay Iyer: we integrate with customer KMS (aws kms, gcp kms, and HSM options) and support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. for logs we can provide per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
[02:18] Alicia Gomez: good. on compatibility: our experiments with open-source stacks like tgi/vllm show performance variability. can you run our eval and show parity metrics?
[02:27] Sanjay Iyer: yes we typically run a parity benchmark in a test tenant. we can run your 2k prompt set, compare outputs for a set of models and report differences and token-cost comparisons. note that small differences in tokenizer or model variants can cause surface-level differences; we focus on downstream metrics.
[02:42] Tom Reed: what's the onboarding timeline for Dedicated? how long to provision GPUs and migrate traffic?
[02:47] Jamie Park: typical pilot setup is 1-2 weeks to provision a test cluster and run evals; a production migration depends on commit size but many customers do a 4-8 week rollout. for Dedicated we have reserved capacity options and burst capacity.
[02:59] Alicia Gomez: cost can you ballpark savings vs openai for high-volume generation?
[03:04] Sanjay Iyer: it varies, but customers targeting cost parity see 30-60% reduction in per-token cost when moving to Dedicated with batching & caching enabled. the biggest wins are for high qps where batching is effective.
[03:19] Alicia Gomez: nice. we do a lot of multi-turn which complicates batching. does caching preserve KV across sessions?
[03:26] Sanjay Iyer: yes, we have prefix/KV caching and sticky routing options. also config to limit cache TTLs for privacy requirements.
[03:35] Nina Patel: audit logs how long are they stored? we need 12 months for certain customers.
[03:40] Jamie Park: we have add-ons for extended log retention; out-of-the-box is shorter but enterprise packages cover 12+ months with secure storage and export options.
[03:48] Tom Reed: compatibility with our vLLM setups can we bring our existing model weights or do we need format conversions?
[03:55] Sanjay Iyer: we support common ONNX/ggml/transformer formats and provide conversion assistance. for some proprietary formats we can help with conversion pipelines. sometimes tokenization differences cause drift; we include tokenizers in our model onboarding.
[04:09] Alicia Gomez: are there differences in deterministic outputs vs openai? we need to ensure few-shot prompts behave similarly.
[04:15] Sanjay Iyer: small differences are expected due to model weights and temperature seeds. our parity process captures distributional metrics and human evals for critical flows. we can also run exact seed matches where supported.
[04:26] Jamie Park: any compliance red flags from your side?
[04:29] Nina Patel: mostly data residency and KMS integration. also need code access controls; if private deployment needed, what does that look like?
[04:36] Sanjay Iyer: private means a customer-managed control plane and optionally an on-prem bundle. we’ve done air-gapped installs for regulated customers; it requires some lead time for ops and networking changes.
[04:48] Tom Reed: how do you handle fallback if dedicated capacity hits limits? we don't want degraded user experience.
[04:53] Sanjay Iyer: smart routing policies you can set fallback to hosted variants or lower-cost model variants and Redwood will route automatically. we also support canary rollouts and automatic failover.
[05:05] Alicia Gomez: perf can you share 99th percentile numbers for multi-turn at seq len 1k?
[05:10] Sanjay Iyer: generally depends on hardware & quantization; for A100/80GB with optimized kernels we see sub-700ms for many 1k seq multi-turns on 99p for some decoder-only models; but we'd run your exact workload in the benchmark for a realistic number.
[05:28] Jamie Park: quick note on pricing we have pay-as-you-go hosted API and reserved capacity for Dedicated, plus enterprise pricing for Private. I'll send the pricing matrix.
[05:36] Alicia Gomez: fantastic. any known migration pitfalls?
[05:39] Sanjay Iyer: tokenizer mismatches and prompt formatting are common. also batching config and kv cache tuning need iteration. we try to automate with migration playbooks and preflight checks.
[05:51] Tom Reed: can we get a sample infra diagram for dedicated deployment and VPC peering details?
[05:55] Jamie Park: yes, i'll include infra diagrams and network requirements in the follow-up email.
[05:59] Nina Patel: we'll need a legal/privacy contact for DPAs and data processing terms.
[06:02] Jamie Park: adding that to next steps.

Recap (final 3 mins):
[06:10] Jamie Park: recap Action: we will send pricing, infra diagram, and provision a test tenant. Sanjay will run parity tests with your 2k prompt set. Nina to share security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence. Follow-up deep-dive on VPC/private the week of 10/12.
[06:30] Alicia Gomez: thanks, that works. any blockers from our side I'll email tom/nina.
[06:36] Jamie Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email and calendar for the deep-dive.
[06:40] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had some mis-heard acronyms (vLLM sometimes transcribed as v-elm) and some punctuation errors. this transcript has been lightly edited for readability but retains original speaker turns and timestamps.
